# AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents and coding assistants

If you are an LLM (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor, etc.) reading this
repository to answer questions about **Uplink** (personal Morpheus API
gateway, formerly PAPIGW), **read this file first**. Generic web knowledge
and hosted-gateway habits often get this product wrong.

## How to load documentation (follow this order)

1. **This file** — hard rules, quick lookup, repo pointers. No network required.
2. **[`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt)** — complete operator + product corpus as
   plain markdown (concat of `docs/` + this file’s priority sections).
3. **[`llms.txt`](llms.txt)** — lightweight page index (title, description, path).
4. **Operator chapters** under [`docs/`](docs/README.md) — human-facing how-to.
5. **Concept / design** (optional depth): [`.ai-docs/UPLINK_CONCEPT.md`](.ai-docs/UPLINK_CONCEPT.md).
6. **Do not invent** live catalog size, bid prices, or contract addresses —
   use the **gateway** feeds
   ([`gateway_models.json`](https://active.mor.org/gateway_models.json),
   [`gateway_bids.json`](https://active.mor.org/gateway_bids.json)) and the
   addresses in [`docs/01-prerequisites.md`](docs/01-prerequisites.md).
   Never default to `active_models.json` / ALL.

Published operator path: clone or browse this repo → `AGENTS.md` → `docs/`.
There is no separate docs host or MCP for Uplink.

## Priority reading

| Topic | Path |
|-------|------|
| Operator guide index | [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md) |
| Prerequisites (wallet, MOR, RPC) | [`docs/01-prerequisites.md`](docs/01-prerequisites.md) |
| Bootstrap (SecretVM / VPS / Railway) | [`docs/02-bootstrap.md`](docs/02-bootstrap.md) |

| Clients / agents (`/v1`) | [`docs/04-clients.md`](docs/04-clients.md) |
| Updates & portability | [`docs/05-updates.md`](docs/05-updates.md) |
| Developers (local / CI / env / layout) | [`docs/06-developers.md`](docs/06-developers.md) |
| Product + SecretVM CTA | [`README.md`](README.md) |

## Hard rules — never break these

0. **Never confuse Uplink with the hosted Morpheus Inference API.**  
   Hosted multi-tenant gateway: [api.mor.org](https://api.mor.org) /
   [apidocs.mor.org](https://apidocs.mor.org).  
   Uplink: **your** single-tenant gateway in front of **your** consumer
   proxy-router (C-Node). Same OpenAI shape (`/v1/chat/completions`),
   different product, wallet, and ops model.

1. **Never confuse Uplink’s public API with the raw proxy-router API.**  
   Clients talk to Uplink with **Bearer `sk-…`**.  
   The C-Node under it uses **HTTP Basic Auth** (`COOKIE_CONTENT`) and needs a
   `session_id` header for remote models — Uplink opens/reuses sessions so
   clients do not. Proxy-router docs live in Morpheus-Lumerin-Node
   (`proxy-router/docs/swagger.yaml`, [nodedocs.mor.org](https://nodedocs.mor.org)).

2. **Never invent contract addresses, chain IDs, or token addresses.**  
   Base mainnet: chain ID `8453`, Diamond
   `0x6aBE1d282f72B474E54527D93b979A4f64d3030a`, MOR
   `0x7431ada8a591c955a994a21710752ef9b882b8e3` — see
   [`docs/01-prerequisites.md`](docs/01-prerequisites.md). For anything else,
   cite nodedocs networks page; do not guess.

3. **Never invent live values** (active model count, bid prices, latency).  
   Use [`gateway_models.json`](https://active.mor.org/gateway_models.json) /
   [`gateway_bids.json`](https://active.mor.org/gateway_bids.json). Never
   default to `active_models.json` / ALL as the Uplink catalog.

4. **Never claim Morpheus “runs the inference.”** Independent providers do;
   Morpheus coordinates the marketplace on Base.

5. **Opening a session escrows MOR; it does not spend it.** Unused stake
   returns on close (subject to daylock rules). Cite
   [`docs/03-gui.md`](docs/03-gui.md#where-is-my-mor) and
   [nodedocs — Where is my MOR?](https://nodedocs.mor.org/ai/where-is-my-mor).

6. **There is no `recover` RPC.** Closing the session is the recovery path.

7. **Do not expose the proxy-router admin port publicly.** Only the TLS
   front (Uplink on `:443` / local `:8080`) should be public. Router `:8082`
   stays on the compose network; `/node/*` is the admin-gated passthrough
   (GET, HEAD, POST and DELETE only), with a block list for routes that
   move funds, open sessions, or change the wallet, users, permissions or
   config (see `internal/api/nodeproxy.go`).
   Consumer nodes need **no inbound `:3333`** — they dial out to providers.

8. **Deploy from GitHub Release assets, not `git clone`, for production.**  
   Three overlays, same GHCR digests: SecretVM
   (`docker-compose.secretvm.deployed.yml`), generic VPS
   (`docker-compose.generic.deployed.yml`), and Railway scaffold
   (`deploy/railway/`, reference asset `docker-compose.railway.deployed.yml`).
   Every image in the assets is digest-pinned. Prefer
   [MorpheusAIs releases/latest](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest)
   over forks. Proxy-router (Lumerin) is **pinned to v7.17.0 by digest**
   (Lumerin `main`, includes #889 gateway caps — **not** Base
   testnet; chain defaults remain mainnet) — never advise `:latest`. Railway: secrets in Railway Secrets only;
   single-replica proxy-router.

9. **Use exact model catalog names** from `GET /v1/models`, Probe, or
   [`gateway_models.json`](https://active.mor.org/gateway_models.json)
   (`ACTIVE_MODELS_URL` default; companion
   `GATEWAY_BIDS_URL` → `https://active.mor.org/gateway_bids.json`).
   Wrong strings fail resolve. Never invent a flashy name; never point
   agents at `active_models.json` / ALL.

10. **Key roles:** Master (`sk-uplink.…`) = inference, plus admin only with
    `MASTER_KEY_ADMIN=true` (default off; never on logout or 2FA
    status/enroll, which need the admin cookie session); Prompt
    (`sk-prompt.…`) = inference only (default for clients); ephemeral =
    named, export/import across wipes. Built-ins derive from `API_KEY_SEED`.

11. **Provider-specific request extras** (e.g. `venice_parameters`,
    `thinking`) are forwarded through Uplink/proxy-router when the client
    sends them. Whether a **provider** honors them is upstream — do not
    blame Uplink for a model that ignores `disable_thinking`.

12. **When uncertain, cite a docs page or say so.** Prefer
    [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt) / [`docs/`](docs/) over guessing.

13. **License / disclaimer:** Source is MIT ([`LICENSE`](LICENSE), ABSGrafx LLC).
    Operator risk language is in [`DISCLAIMER.md`](DISCLAIMER.md). Third-party
    notices (including go-ethereum LGPL) are in [`NOTICE`](NOTICE). Do not claim
    Uplink is a pure-MIT binary stack without mentioning NOTICE.

## Repository map


## When writing code in this repo

- Public inference auth: **Bearer `sk-…`** on `/v1/*`.
- Do not hard-code contract addresses; keep them in compose/config.
- Prefer release-asset deploy instructions for operators; `docker compose`
  local is for development.
- Compose templates and env examples must pass
  `bash scripts/deploy-assets.sh pr` (the release uses the same script).
- Feature work: branch → PR → `main` (release tags cut on merge to `main`).

## Regenerating the corpus

After editing operator docs:

```bash
./scripts/gen-llms.sh
```

That refreshes `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` from `docs/`, `deploy/*/README.md`, and this file.

# Uplink — Disclaimer

**Operator:** ABSGrafx LLC (South Dakota, USA)  
**Software:** Uplink (this repository) — a personal, self-hosted gateway to the
Morpheus network  
**License:** MIT — see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)

Last updated: 2026-08-11

This is not a hosted service contract and not a bank. You run Uplink on
**your** machine with **your** wallet. Please read before you fund it or share
an API key.

---

## Heads up (self-custody)

- Uplink is **self-custodial**. The wallet private key and `API_KEY_SEED` live
  in **your** environment. We cannot recover lost keys, seed, passwords, or
  daylocked MOR. No one can.
- Prefer a **dedicated** consumer wallet with only what you need for sessions
  and gas — not your main holdings.

## What you are running

- **Experimental software**, provided **AS IS**, with no uptime, accuracy, or
  fitness guarantee.
- A **single-tenant** gateway: one wallet, one session pool. Any Prompt or
  ephemeral API key can open sessions and **escrow / lock MOR** from that
  wallet. Treat every inference key as authority to lock this wallet's MOR.
- Admin login (and the Master key with `MASTER_KEY_ADMIN=true`, except on
  the session-only logout and 2FA status/enroll routes) can reach
  `/admin/*` and the `/node/*` router passthrough. The passthrough refuses
  routes that send or approve funds, open sessions, create providers, models
  or bids, change the wallet, router users, permissions or config, or access
  router files, or make the router contact a caller-chosen address. Protect admin access
  like the wallet.
- You must terminate **TLS** yourself (SecretVM / Caddy / etc.). Do not expose
  Uplink or the router admin port without HTTPS and strong secrets.

## Inference and privacy

- Prompts and completions go to **independent Morpheus providers** (and their
  upstreams). Do not put secrets, keys, or data you cannot afford to leak into
  prompts.
- Model quality, availability, and whether vendor extras (e.g. Venice
  parameters) are honored are **upstream** — not controlled by Uplink.

## Not the hosted API

- Uplink is **not** [api.mor.org](https://api.mor.org) / the Morpheus
  Marketplace hosted gateway. Different product, different risk, your ops.
- Morpheus coordinates a marketplace; providers run inference. See
  [nodedocs.mor.org](https://nodedocs.mor.org).

## No warranty / liability

THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
IMPLIED. TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW, ABSGrafx LLC AND ITS
CONTRIBUTORS ARE NOT LIABLE FOR ANY DAMAGES ARISING FROM USE OF UPLINK,
INCLUDING LOSS OF MOR, KEYS, DATA, PROFITS, OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION — WHETHER
FROM SOFTWARE BUGS, MISCONFIGURATION, THIRD-PARTY PROVIDERS, NETWORK FAILURE,
OR YOUR OWN OPERATIONAL CHOICES.

Forks and self-built copies are governed by the MIT license alone. This
disclaimer is how we ask operators to understand the product; it does not
replace advice from your own counsel if you redistribute or embed Uplink
commercially.

## Contact

| For | Reach |
|-----|--------|
| Bugs / features | [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/issues) |
| Security disclosure / license | Use a private channel to the maintainer (ABSGrafx) |

By running Uplink, you acknowledge self-custody, third-party inference, and
the AS IS nature of this software.

<h1 align="center">Uplink</h1>

<p align="center">
  <strong>Your personal gateway to the Morpheus decentralized AI network.</strong>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="LICENSE">MIT</a> ·
  <a href="DISCLAIMER.md">Disclaimer</a> ·
  <a href="NOTICE">NOTICE</a>
  &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <a href="docs/README.md">Operator guide</a> ·
  <a href="docs/04-clients.md">Clients</a> ·
  <a href="docs/06-developers.md">Developers</a>
  &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <a href="AGENTS.md">Agents</a>
</p>

> Self-custodial and experimental: you hold the wallet keys; any Prompt key can
> lock MOR on that wallet; prompts go to third-party providers. Read
> [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md) before you fund a box or share a key.

## What it is

The hosted Morpheus API ([api.mor.org](https://api.mor.org)) is a **shared**
gateway — many users, pooled sessions, credits billed by Morpheus.

**Uplink is the opposite:** *your* OpenAI-compatible HTTPS front door on *your*
machine, backed by *your* consumer proxy-router (C-Node) and *your* wallet.

- Same shape clients already know: `POST /v1/chat/completions`, embeddings,
  `GET /v1/models`, Bearer `sk-…` keys
- Sessions open and reuse automatically (model name → on-chain session)
- On boot it reuses still-valid open sessions and closes expired or duplicate ones before opening any. A graceful `docker stop` closes every open session on the wallet, including sessions for models not in the catalog and, on a shared wallet, the other client's sessions; the stake is returned (a lock, not a loss). `CLOSE_SESSIONS_ON_EXIT=false` opts out. Use a dedicated wallet ([details](docs/06-developers.md#sessions-across-restarts))
- Admin GUI at `/gui` — balances, keys, Probe, usage
- You pay providers in MOR from the wallet you fund — no multi-tenant credits

## Get running (SecretVM)

**Fastest path:** [SecretVM](https://docs.scrt.network/) (Secret Labs) → paste
the release compose → Encrypted Secrets → fund → Probe → point a client at
`/v1`. Do **not** `git clone` for production — use the
[latest release](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest).

| Step | Do this |
|------|---------|
| **1. Box** | Create a SecretVM that accepts Docker Compose + Encrypted Secrets. |
| **2. Compose** | Paste **`docker-compose.secretvm.deployed.yml`** from the [latest release](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest). |
| **3. Secrets** | Fill Encrypted Secrets (block below) — **operator fillables** (wallet / RPC / cookie / admin / seed / `WEB_PUBLIC_URL`). |
| **4. Deploy** | Start the VM; wait until `uplink` is healthy (proxy-router has no container healthcheck), then check that the GUI Status line reads Healthy. |
| **5. GUI** | Open `https://<host>/gui/` → `admin` / your `ADMIN_PASSWORD`. |
| **6. Fund** | On **Status**, copy the wallet → send a little **ETH** + **MOR** on Base. |
| **7. Use** | **Probe** once, then put the **Prompt** key in any OpenAI client with base URL `https://<host>/v1`. |

<details>
<summary><strong>Encrypted Secrets (copy / paste)</strong></summary>

```bash
WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY=0xYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY
ETH_NODE_ADDRESS=https://base-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_ALCHEMY_KEY
COOKIE_CONTENT=admin:YOUR_STRONG_PASSWORD
ADMIN_PASSWORD=YOUR_GUI_PASSWORD
API_KEY_SEED=PASTE_openssl_rand_hex_32_HERE
WEB_PUBLIC_URL=https://your-vm-name.vm.scrtlabs.com
```

`openssl rand -hex 32` for the seed. Prefer a **dedicated** consumer wallet.
The SecretVM form has exactly these **six** fields (`env.secretvm.example` is the same six). Tunables are **not** Encrypted Secrets: SecretVM keeps them in the compose `configs:` block; generic and local compose take them as env-overridable `${VAR:-default}` defaults, while Railway does not run compose and applies none of them (see the Railway steps below and [docs/06-developers.md](docs/06-developers.md#environment-variables)):
- **Uplink** (`uplink_bake_env` / Uplink process): `ACTIVE_MODELS_URL`, `GATEWAY_BIDS_URL`, `SESSION_DURATION_SECONDS`, `SESSION_FAILOVER`, `UPLINK_PROVIDER_COOLDOWN_SECONDS`, `HOUSEKEEPING`, and the `UPLINK_RESET_2FA` break-glass; wiring defaults `UPLINK_LISTEN`, `ROUTER_URL`, `DATA_DIR`, `USAGE_PRUNE_DAYS`, `CLOSE_SESSIONS_ON_EXIT`. Diamond / `ETH_NODE_CHAIN_ID` are **not** Uplink operator knobs.
- **Router** (`router_network_env` / proxy-router only; godotenv -- process env wins): `PROXY_STORE_CHAT_CONTEXT`, `PROXY_FORWARD_CHAT_CONTEXT`, `LOG_LEVEL_APP`/`TCP`/`ETH_RPC`, `ETH_NODE_CHAIN_ID`, `ETH_NODE_USE_SUBSCRIPTIONS`, `BLOCKSCOUT_API_URL`, `DIAMOND_CONTRACT_ADDRESS`, `MOR_TOKEN_ADDRESS`. Never put router `PROXY_*` / `LOG_LEVEL_*` into Uplink bake docs.
Full walkthrough (and plain Docker VPS): [docs/02-bootstrap.md](docs/02-bootstrap.md).

</details>

**Done when:** GUI at `/gui/`, wallet funded with ETH+MOR on Base, Probe succeeds, OpenAI client hits `https://<host>/v1` with a Prompt key.

### Generic VPS

Same GHCR images (`ghcr.io/morpheusais/uplink` from the [latest release](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest)) and Lumerin pin as SecretVM. Release asset: **`docker-compose.generic.deployed.yml`** (+ `env.generic.example`). Full walkthrough: [docs/02-bootstrap.md#first-start--generic-vps](docs/02-bootstrap.md#first-start--generic-vps).

| Step | Do this |
|------|---------|
| **1. DNS / ports** | Point A/AAAA at the box; open **80** and **443**. |
| **2. Compose** | Download **`docker-compose.generic.deployed.yml`** (+ `env.generic.example` → `.env`) from the [latest release](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest). |
| **3. Secrets** | Fill `.env`: `PUBLIC_HOST` + the operator fillables (wallet / RPC / cookie / admin / seed / `WEB_PUBLIC_URL`) — never commit. |
| **4. Deploy** | `docker compose -f docker-compose.generic.deployed.yml --env-file .env up -d` (Caddy + LE). |
| **5. GUI → fund → Probe** | Open `https://$PUBLIC_HOST/gui/` → fund ETH+MOR on Base → Probe → Prompt key at `/v1`. |

**Done when:** same as SecretVM — GUI, funded wallet, Probe OK, client on `https://<host>/v1`.

### Railway scaffold

Supported Uplink hosts are **SecretVM**, **generic VPS**, and **this in-repo Railway scaffold** only. Do not follow third-party consumer-gateway Railway stacks (different images/vars such as DOMAIN / PUBLIC_ORIGIN).

Same image pair. The [latest release](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest) ships a digest-pinned reference **`docker-compose.railway.deployed.yml`** (+ `env.railway.example`); Railway does not run compose itself, so copy its image digests and variables into the Railway services (scaffold: [`deploy/railway/`](deploy/railway/)). Checklist: [docs/02-bootstrap.md#first-start--railway](docs/02-bootstrap.md#first-start--railway) · [deploy/railway/README.md](deploy/railway/README.md).

| Step | Do this |
|------|---------|
| **1. Project** | Create Railway project: uplink + proxy-router on a private network. |
| **2. Images** | Use the digests from `docker-compose.railway.deployed.yml` for `ghcr.io/morpheusais/uplink` and Lumerin — not bare `:latest`. |
| **3. Secrets + vars** | Set the operator fillables (wallet / admin / seed / cookie / RPC / `WEB_PUBLIC_URL`) as **Railway Secrets**. Railway applies no compose defaults, so also set the active lines of `env.railway.example` as plain service variables: `PROXY_STORE_CHAT_CONTEXT=false` (unset stores chat context), `LOG_LEVEL_APP=warn`, `ETH_NODE_CHAIN_ID=8453` and the chain addresses on proxy-router. |
| **4. Replicas** | `proxy-router` replicas = **1** (wallet-bearing). |
| **5. Edge** | Public HTTPS → uplink `:8080` only; open `/gui/` → turn 2FA on (Security tab, recommended) → fund → Probe → `/v1`. |

**Done when:** same as SecretVM — GUI, funded wallet, Probe OK, client on `https://<host>/v1`.

```bash
curl -s https://YOUR_HOST/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prompt.…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"REPLACE_WITH_PROBE_NAME","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":64}'
```

Use an **exact** model name from Probe / `GET /v1/models` / the gateway
catalog — do **not** hardcode a flashy name, and do **not** treat generic
[active.mor.org](https://active.mor.org) or `active_models.json` / ALL feeds
as the catalog. Defaults:

| Env (baked) | Default |
|-------------|---------|
| `ACTIVE_MODELS_URL` | `https://active.mor.org/gateway_models.json` |
| `GATEWAY_BIDS_URL` | `https://active.mor.org/gateway_bids.json` |

Images: `ghcr.io/morpheusais/uplink` ([latest release](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest)). Release compose **digest-pins Uplink and proxy-router (Lumerin) v7.17.0**
(Lumerin `main` / #889 caps — **not** Base testnet) — not
`:latest`. More clients: [docs/04-clients.md](docs/04-clients.md).

## Things worth knowing

- **Not the hosted APIGW.** No Morpheus credits account, no shared pool with
  strangers. One wallet, one gateway, your ops.
- **Any Prompt / ephemeral key can lock MOR** from that wallet as session
  stake (returned, held at most until the next UTC day). Keep Master off
  shared machines.
- **Built-in keys survive a wipe** if you keep the same `API_KEY_SEED`.
  Rotating it also invalidates the 2FA secret and recovery codes; the way
  back is one restart with `UPLINK_RESET_2FA=true`.
  Generated (ephemeral) keys and local usage history do not — export them if
  you care. Sessions and stake live on-chain with the wallet.
- **Deploy from release assets**, not a git checkout. Every image in them is
  digest-pinned, Uplink and **proxy-router v7.17.0** included (not `:latest`).
- **Gateway catalog only:** `ACTIVE_MODELS_URL` →
  `https://active.mor.org/gateway_models.json`, `GATEWAY_BIDS_URL` →
  `https://active.mor.org/gateway_bids.json`. Never default to
  `active_models.json` / ALL.
- **Admin 2FA** (TOTP) is an on/off switch on the Security tab, off by
  default on every deploy (first login is password only). We recommend
  turning it on: the switch runs the enrollment (QR code, confirm a code)
  and issues 10 single-use recovery codes, shown once; from then on login
  needs a TOTP or recovery code. The switch is kept in `DATA_DIR`, so it
  survives restarts and redeploys. The Security tab shows how many codes
  are left and can regenerate them, reset 2FA (wipe and re-enroll; 2FA
  stays on) or turn it off (password plus a code; signs out every session).
  No environment variable turns 2FA on.
  Emergency recovery when locked out: one restart with
  `UPLINK_RESET_2FA=true` (2FA comes back off).
  [Details](docs/06-developers.md#admin-2fa-and-recovery-codes)
- **Only expose the gateway** (HTTPS). The router admin port stays private.
- **`/node/*` router passthrough** takes GET, HEAD, POST and DELETE only,
  is admin-gated, and refuses routes that send or approve funds, open
  sessions, create providers, models or bids, change the wallet, router
  users, permissions or config, access router files, or make the router
  contact a caller-chosen address (403, audited). Reads (GET, HEAD) pass
  through, wallet, router-user and config reads included. [Details](docs/06-developers.md#router-access-and-restart-safety)

Operator chapters (wallet → GUI → clients → updates): **[docs/README.md](docs/README.md)**.  
Building / CI / env / layout: **[docs/06-developers.md](docs/06-developers.md)**.

<!-- source: docs/README.md -->

# Uplink operator guide

**Uplink** is your personal gateway to the [Morpheus](https://mor.org) network: an OpenAI-compatible HTTPS endpoint backed by your own consumer proxy-router (C-Node) and wallet.

**Recommended host:** [SecretVM](https://docs.scrt.network/) (Secret Labs) —
encrypted secrets + platform TLS. Root README has the fast CTA:
**[Get running on SecretVM](../README.md#get-running-secretvm)**.

AI agents: read root [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) first (hard rules + [`llms-full.txt`](../llms-full.txt)).

**Before you fund anything:** [DISCLAIMER.md](../DISCLAIMER.md) (self-custody, shared wallet, third-party inference). License: [MIT](../LICENSE).

## Fast path (SecretVM)

2. [Bootstrap → First start — SecretVM](02-bootstrap.md#first-start--secretvm) — release compose + Encrypted Secrets  
3. [GUI](03-gui.md) — login, fund Status wallet, **Probe** once  
4. [Apps & agents](04-clients.md) — base URL `https://<host>/v1` + Prompt key  

Open [Updates](05-updates.md) when a new release ships. Other hosts share the
same GHCR image pair:

- **Generic VPS** (Caddy + LE) — [Bootstrap](02-bootstrap.md#first-start--generic-vps) · [deploy/generic](../deploy/generic/README.md)
- **Railway** (scaffold) — [Bootstrap](02-bootstrap.md#first-start--railway) · [deploy/railway](../deploy/railway/README.md)

SecretVM overlay notes: [deploy/secretvm](../deploy/secretvm/README.md). Local
build / CI / env tables: [Developers](06-developers.md).

## Quick checklist

- [ ] Compose from **[latest release](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest)** (no git clone) — or Railway scaffold under `deploy/railway/`
- [ ] Six operator fillables set (SecretVM Encrypted Secrets / generic `.env` + `PUBLIC_HOST` / Railway Secrets) including `WEB_PUBLIC_URL`
- [ ] `/gui` login works
- [ ] Wallet funded (ETH + MOR on Base)
- [ ] Probe returns a completion
- [ ] Client: `…/v1` + Prompt/ephemeral key + exact model name

# 1. Prerequisites

[← Guide home](README.md) · [Next: Bootstrap →](02-bootstrap.md)

What you need before compose. Skip anything you already have.

Read the short [DISCLAIMER](../DISCLAIMER.md) first — self-custody, experimental software, and the fact that **any inference key can escrow MOR** from this wallet.

| Need | Why | Links |
|------|-----|--------|
| **Host that runs Docker Compose + HTTPS** | Runs Uplink + proxy-router + TLS | **Preferred:** [SecretVM](https://docs.scrt.network/) (Secret Labs — Encrypted Secrets + platform TLS). Alternate: any Docker VPS ([Hetzner](https://www.hetzner.com/), [DigitalOcean](https://www.digitalocean.com/), …) or [Phala](https://cloud.phala.network) / [dstack](https://github.com/Dstack-TEE/dstack). Pull compose from [releases](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest) — no git clone. |
| **External wallet (Rabby / MetaMask)** | You fund the *consumer* address; Uplink is not custodial | [Rabby](https://rabby.io/), [MetaMask](https://metamask.io/) |
| **ETH on Base** | Gas for open / close / reclaim | [Base](https://www.base.org/) |
| **MOR on Base** | Escrowed when sessions open | Token `0x7431ada8a591c955a994a21710752ef9b882b8e3` — [Uniswap ETH→MOR](https://app.uniswap.org/swap?chain=base&inputCurrency=ETH&outputCurrency=0x7431ada8a591c955a994a21710752ef9b882b8e3) |
| **Base HTTPS RPC** | Chain reads/writes | [Alchemy](https://www.alchemy.com/) or [Infura](https://www.infura.io/) → Base mainnet → `https://base-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/…` |
| **Strong passwords + seed** | Admin GUI + API key derivation | `openssl rand -hex 32` |

**Base mainnet facts:** chain ID `8453` · Diamond `0x6aBE1d282f72B474E54527D93b979A4f64d3030a` · catalog [active.mor.org](https://active.mor.org)

<!-- source: docs/02-bootstrap.md -->

# 2. Bootstrap

[← Prerequisites](01-prerequisites.md) · [Guide home](README.md) · [Next: GUI →](03-gui.md)

First boot → funded wallet → GUI login. **No git clone** — download the published compose from the [latest release](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest) and pull images from `ghcr.io`.

**Default path is SecretVM** ([Secret Labs](https://docs.scrt.network/)). Use
generic VPS if you already run your own Docker + TLS. **Railway** is a
scaffold overlay (same image pair; secrets in Railway Secrets only; the
release ships a digest-pinned reference compose for it).
Supported hosts: SecretVM, generic VPS, and this scaffold only -- not third-party
consumer-gateway Railway (no DOMAIN / PUBLIC_ORIGIN operator fields).

---

## Pick a compose path

Three overlays, **same GHCR image pair** (digest-pinned uplink + stock
proxy-router **v7.17.0**). Pick the skin that matches your host:

| Path | Best when | Release / scaffold |
|------|-----------|----------------|
| **SecretVM (recommended)** | Fastest first run — Encrypted Secrets + platform TLS (Traefik) | `docker-compose.secretvm.deployed.yml` + `env.secretvm.example` |
| **Generic VPS** | You already have a box / Phala / dstack — Caddy + Let’s Encrypt / `.env` | `docker-compose.generic.deployed.yml` + `env.generic.example` |
| **Railway (scaffold)** | Railway HTTPS edge; secrets in Railway Secrets only; single-replica proxy-router | `docker-compose.railway.deployed.yml` + `env.railway.example` (reference; Railway does not run compose) + [operator checklist](../deploy/railway/README.md) |

Images (already named in the YAML): `ghcr.io/morpheusais/uplink@sha…` (digest-pinned) · `ghcr.io/morpheusais/morpheus-lumerin-node:v7.17.0@sha256:da1baa55299133ad63e2e590bd8cc1e95772ff81f4b44e2aa34cabe682e9a14d` (digest-pinned in compose). Every image in the release compose is digest-pinned; none is `:latest`.

**Pin note:** tag `v7.17.0` is **Lumerin `main`** (includes [#889](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Lumerin-Node/pull/889) gateway caps) — **not** Base testnet. Chain ID / Diamond / MOR come from compose env and still default to **Base mainnet** (`8453`, Diamond `0x6aBE1d282f72B474E54527D93b979A4f64d3030a`, MOR `0x7431ada8a591c955a994a21710752ef9b882b8e3`).

**CA bundle note:** the proxy-router `v7.17.0` image ships a refreshed CA bundle that removes several older roots (for example emSign, Comodo AAA, Entrust Root G4, TrustCor, E-Tugra, SECOM RootCA1/RootCA3, SwissSign Silver G2, Hongkong Post Root CA 1, SecureSign RootCA11 and an older Firmaprofesional root). A custom `ETH_NODE_ADDRESS` or other upstream whose certificate chains to a removed root will fail TLS after the upgrade. The default endpoints in the compose files were checked against the new bundle on 2026-10-27.

Overlay detail: [deploy/secretvm](../deploy/secretvm/README.md) · [deploy/generic](../deploy/generic/README.md) · [deploy/railway](../deploy/railway/README.md).

Root README CTA: **[Get running on SecretVM](../README.md#get-running-secretvm)**.

---

## SecretVM disk hygiene

Small SecretVM instances have about 20 GB of disk. The published compose files
use Docker's `json-file` logging with rotation enabled by default at `20m` x 3
files per service, limiting retained container logs while keeping a short
history.

The Status tab (and Support section) shows free space for `/` and `DATA_DIR`
from inside the uplink process. When free space is below **2 GiB** or **15%**,
a warn banner appears. Admins can clear older usage-history rows via
**Clear older usage history** (`POST /admin/disk/prune-usage`, typed confirm
`PRUNE_USAGE`, retention default 30 days via `USAGE_PRUNE_DAYS`) — this never
deletes API keys or Docker logs. Docker json-file logs stay rotation-bounded;
if Status still warns after prune, the panel shows copy-paste host
`docker compose … --force-recreate --no-deps` commands (no auto-run).

This does **not** auto-wipe volumes. Do not schedule `docker system prune -a`
as a cron job, and do not hand-delete `*-json.log` files; investigate storage
and use the documented update path instead.

---

## Secrets

Generate a seed once: `openssl rand -hex 32`

<details>
<summary><strong>SecretVM — copyable secrets</strong></summary>

Paste into Encrypted Secrets (or the auto-built form). Replace the placeholders.

```bash
WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY=0xYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY
ETH_NODE_ADDRESS=https://base-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_ALCHEMY_KEY
COOKIE_CONTENT=admin:YOUR_STRONG_PASSWORD
ADMIN_PASSWORD=YOUR_GUI_PASSWORD
API_KEY_SEED=PASTE_openssl_rand_hex_32_HERE
WEB_PUBLIC_URL=https://your-vm-name.vm.scrtlabs.com
```

**Only these six** belong in Encrypted Secrets. SecretVM scrapes **every**
`environment:` key (literals too), so tunables stay in compose `configs:`
(change via code / compose only -- not operator forms):

> To change a SecretVM tunable, edit the `configs:` block
> (`uplink_bake_env` / `router_network_env`) in
> `deploy/secretvm/docker-compose.yml` (or your downloaded
> `docker-compose.secretvm.deployed.yml`). SecretVM turns every `${...}` in
> the compose file into an operator prompt, and the form deliberately stays
> at the six secrets, so SecretVM has no `${VAR:-default}` overrides.

- **Uplink** (`uplink_bake_env`): `SESSION_DURATION_SECONDS=600`,
  `SESSION_FAILOVER=true`, `UPLINK_PROVIDER_COOLDOWN_SECONDS=600`,
  `ACTIVE_MODELS_URL` / `GATEWAY_BIDS_URL`,
  `HOUSEKEEPING=true`, and master key admin access fixed off
  (`MASTER_KEY_ADMIN=false`). Wiring defaults (`UPLINK_LISTEN`, `ROUTER_URL`,
  `DATA_DIR`, `USAGE_PRUNE_DAYS`,
  `CLOSE_SESSIONS_ON_EXIT`) are Uplink process env too. Diamond /
  `ETH_NODE_CHAIN_ID` are **not** Uplink operator knobs.
  2FA is turned on in the GUI, not here (see [2FA](#admin-2fa-switch)).
  2FA emergency recovery: add `UPLINK_RESET_2FA=true` to `uplink_bake_env`,
  redeploy once, then remove it and redeploy
  ([details](06-developers.md#admin-2fa-and-recovery-codes)).
- **Router** (`router_network_env`; godotenv -- process env wins):
  `PROXY_STORE_CHAT_CONTEXT`, `PROXY_FORWARD_CHAT_CONTEXT`,
  `LOG_LEVEL_APP` / `LOG_LEVEL_TCP` / `LOG_LEVEL_ETH_RPC`,
  `ETH_NODE_CHAIN_ID`, `ETH_NODE_USE_SUBSCRIPTIONS`, `BLOCKSCOUT_API_URL`,
  `DIAMOND_CONTRACT_ADDRESS`, `MOR_TOKEN_ADDRESS`. Never put router
  `PROXY_*` / `LOG_LEVEL_*` into Uplink bake.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Generic VPS — copyable `.env`</strong></summary>

Save as `.env` next to the compose file. Replace the placeholders. `PUBLIC_HOST` must match DNS.

```bash
PUBLIC_HOST=uplink.yourdomain.com

WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY=0xYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY
ETH_NODE_ADDRESS=https://base-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_ALCHEMY_KEY
COOKIE_CONTENT=admin:YOUR_STRONG_PASSWORD
ADMIN_PASSWORD=YOUR_GUI_PASSWORD
API_KEY_SEED=PASTE_openssl_rand_hex_32_HERE
WEB_PUBLIC_URL=https://uplink.yourdomain.com
```

Tunables are env-overridable compose defaults (`${VAR:-default}`): unset
keeps the default; set one in `.env` to override (the list is in
[06](06-developers.md#environment-variables)). Master key admin access
defaults to off (`MASTER_KEY_ADMIN=false`); turning it on weakens admin
security. 2FA is turned on in the GUI (see [2FA](#admin-2fa-switch)).
2FA emergency recovery: `UPLINK_RESET_2FA=true` in `.env` for one restart,
then remove it. Keep ownership separate:
**Uplink** session/catalog/housekeeping (+ wiring defaults);
**Router** `PROXY_*` / `LOG_LEVEL_*` / chain / Diamond / MOR. Never describe
router `PROXY_*` / `LOG_LEVEL_*` as Uplink knobs.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Railway — secrets only in Railway Secrets</strong></summary>

Do **not** put wallet/admin/seed/cookie/RPC/`WEB_PUBLIC_URL` material in
`railway.toml`, image labels, build args, or committed compose. Set these
six as **Railway Secrets** / vars (same surface as SecretVM / generic):

- `WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY`
- `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
- `API_KEY_SEED`
- `COOKIE_CONTENT`
- RPC credentials (`ETH_NODE_ADDRESS` and any provider key material)
- `WEB_PUBLIC_URL` (Railway HTTPS origin)

Railway does not run compose, so no compose default applies there: an
unset variable takes the process's own default, which can differ from the
compose value (table in [deploy/railway/README.md](../deploy/railway/README.md#unset-on-railway)).
Set plain values as Railway Variables (Uplink vs router ownership stays
separate; see SecretVM block above). On proxy-router set
`PROXY_STORE_CHAT_CONTEXT=false` (unset stores chat context),
`LOG_LEVEL_APP=warn`, `ETH_NODE_CHAIN_ID=8453` and the chain addresses from
`env.railway.example`. Then turn 2FA on in the GUI (recommended; see
[2FA](#admin-2fa-switch)), and keep `DATA_DIR` on a persistent volume so the
2FA switch and enrollment survive redeploys. Full checklist:
[deploy/railway/README.md](../deploy/railway/README.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Var ownership (Uplink vs router)</strong></summary>

Product rule: **form stays six**; tunables are not Encrypted Secrets. SecretVM keeps them in compose `configs:`; generic and local compose take them as env-overridable defaults (`${VAR:-default}`); Railway does not run compose and applies none of them.

| Bucket | Where | Vars |
|--------|-------|------|
| **Minimum to run** | Operator fillables everywhere | `WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY`, `ETH_NODE_ADDRESS`, `COOKIE_CONTENT`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `API_KEY_SEED`, `WEB_PUBLIC_URL` |
| **Uplink tunable / additional** | Uplink process only (`uplink_bake_env` / `internal/config`) | `ACTIVE_MODELS_URL`, `GATEWAY_BIDS_URL`, `SESSION_DURATION_SECONDS`, `SESSION_FAILOVER`, `UPLINK_PROVIDER_COOLDOWN_SECONDS`, `UPLINK_PROVIDER_EXCLUDE`, `HOUSEKEEPING`; long-job limits `UPLINK_SESSION_DURATION_MAX`, `UPLINK_FORWARD_IDLE_SECONDS`, `UPLINK_SESSION_IDLE_GRACE_SECONDS`, `UPLINK_INFLIGHT_MAX`, `UPLINK_LONG_PER_KEY_MODEL`, `UPLINK_LONG_PER_KEY`, `UPLINK_LONG_SESSIONS_MAX`, `UPLINK_OPENS_PER_KEY_MODEL_HOUR`, log level `UPLINK_LOG_LEVEL` (process env only, defaults fit; see [Long jobs](06-developers.md#long-jobs)); wiring defaults `UPLINK_LISTEN`, `ROUTER_URL`, `DATA_DIR`, `USAGE_PRUNE_DAYS`, `CLOSE_SESSIONS_ON_EXIT` |
| **Router tunable / additional** | proxy-router only (`router_network_env`; godotenv -- process env wins) | `PROXY_STORE_CHAT_CONTEXT`, `PROXY_FORWARD_CHAT_CONTEXT`, `LOG_LEVEL_APP` / `TCP` / `ETH_RPC`, `ETH_NODE_CHAIN_ID`, `ETH_NODE_USE_SUBSCRIPTIONS`, `BLOCKSCOUT_API_URL`, `DIAMOND_CONTRACT_ADDRESS`, `MOR_TOKEN_ADDRESS` |

Diamond / `ETH_NODE_CHAIN_ID` may exist in Uplink config defaults but are **not** Uplink operator knobs. Never put router `PROXY_*` / `LOG_LEVEL_*` into Uplink bake docs.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>What each required var does</strong></summary>

| Var | Used by | Notes |
|-----|---------|--------|
| `WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY` | Router only | Prefer a **dedicated** consumer wallet; fund from Rabby/MetaMask. Uplink holds no key; stake reclaim runs via the router API. |
| `ETH_NODE_ADDRESS` | Router only | Base HTTPS RPC. Uplink reads chain state through the router API. |
| `COOKIE_CONTENT` | Router + Uplink | Router `user:password`. Uplink uses it to call the router over the internal network; the router port is never published. |
| `ADMIN_PASSWORD` | Uplink | GUI login (username is always `admin`). |
| `API_KEY_SEED` | Uplink | Hex seed for Master/Prompt. Keep it; rotating changes both built-in keys and invalidates the 2FA secret and recovery codes (way back: `UPLINK_RESET_2FA=true`, see [06](06-developers.md#admin-2fa-and-recovery-codes)). |
| `WEB_PUBLIC_URL` | Router (+ Uplink) | Public HTTPS origin (`https://….vm.scrtlabs.com`, `https://$PUBLIC_HOST`, or Railway URL). |
| `PUBLIC_HOST` | Caddy (generic only) | DNS name for Let’s Encrypt (platform-specific; not one of the six). |

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Session stake (locks, not spends)</strong></summary>

A session stake is locked while the session runs and is returned to this
wallet, held at most until the next UTC day. Sessions cost ETH gas. Uplink
only opens staking-mode sessions (`directPayment` is always false). Use a
dedicated wallet: the boot reconcile and a graceful stop act on every open
session of the wallet (see [06-developers](06-developers.md#sessions-across-restarts)).

</details>

---

## First start — SecretVM

1. Create a SecretVM that accepts Docker Compose + encrypted secrets.
2. Download **`docker-compose.secretvm.deployed.yml`** from the [latest release](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest) and paste it as the VM compose.
3. Fill Encrypted Secrets from the SecretVM block above (**six keys only**, including `WEB_PUBLIC_URL=https://<vm-host>`).
   `WEB_PUBLIC_URL` must be exactly the scheme + host you open the GUI at (update it on a redeploy to a new host); otherwise admin changes are refused and the Status page warns.
4. Deploy. Wait until `uplink` is healthy (proxy-router has no container
   healthcheck); after login, the GUI Status line should read Healthy.
5. Open `https://<that-host>/gui/` — `admin` / your `ADMIN_PASSWORD`.
6. Turn 2FA on (recommended): Security tab → 2FA switch → scan the QR
   code, confirm a code, and save the 10 recovery codes (shown once).
   See [2FA](#admin-2fa-switch).

---

## First start — generic VPS

DNS A/AAAA → this machine; ports **80** and **443** open. Then:

```bash
mkdir -p uplink && cd uplink

curl -fsSL -O https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest/download/docker-compose.generic.deployed.yml
curl -fsSL -o .env https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest/download/env.generic.example

# Edit .env — fill PUBLIC_HOST + the six required fillables (see Secrets above)
nano .env   # or your editor

docker compose -f docker-compose.generic.deployed.yml --env-file .env up -d
```

Open `https://$PUBLIC_HOST/gui/` and turn 2FA on with the switch on the
Security tab (recommended; off by default, as on every deploy).
`WEB_PUBLIC_URL` must be exactly the scheme + host you open the GUI at (update it on a redeploy to a new host); otherwise admin changes are refused and the Status page warns.

---

## First start — Railway

Scaffold — the release's `docker-compose.railway.deployed.yml` is the
reference (same digests as SecretVM/generic); single-replica
proxy-router. Full step→done checklist:
**[deploy/railway/README.md](../deploy/railway/README.md)**.

1. Create a Railway project with uplink + proxy-router on a private network.
2. Set secret-class vars as **Railway Secrets** only (see Secrets above).
3. Use the uplink and router digests from `docker-compose.railway.deployed.yml` — not bare `:latest`.
4. Replicas = **1** for wallet-bearing `proxy-router`.
5. Confirm only uplink is public (`:8080` behind Railway HTTPS).
6. Open `https://<public>/gui/`, turn 2FA on with the switch on the
   Security tab (recommended; off by default), then fund wallet → Probe
   (same as other hosts).

Done when GUI login works and Probe returns a completion.

---

## Admin 2FA switch

2FA (TOTP) is an operator choice in the GUI, the same on SecretVM,
generic, Railway and local: there is no environment variable for it.

- **Default off.** The first login is password only. While 2FA is off the
  Security tab shows a short note recommending turning it on; nothing is
  forced.
- **Turn on:** Security tab → 2FA switch. Scan the QR code (or enter the
  secret), confirm a code, and save the 10 recovery codes (shown once).
  2FA is on only once a code is confirmed; from then on every login needs a
  TOTP or recovery code.
- **Turn off:** the switch asks for the password plus a current TOTP or
  recovery code. It removes the secret and recovery codes and signs out
  every session; login is password only again.
- **Reset lockdown:** after a Reset the switch stays on, and the next
  password login gets 403 on every admin route except 2FA status,
  enrollment and logout until a new enrollment is confirmed.
- **Persistent:** the switch is stored with the 2FA state in `DATA_DIR`
  (`uplink-state.json`), so it survives restarts and redeploys. Keep
  `DATA_DIR` on a persistent volume.
- **Emergency recovery** (authenticator and recovery codes lost):
  `UPLINK_RESET_2FA=true` for one restart wipes 2FA and all sessions; 2FA
  comes back off. Remove the variable, log in with the password and turn
  2FA on again ([details](06-developers.md#admin-2fa-and-recovery-codes)).

---

## Fund the consumer wallet

On **Status**, copy the wallet address. From Rabby/MetaMask on Base, send:

1. A little **ETH** (gas).
2. Enough **MOR** for sessions you will open (see [how close vs expire affects stake](03-gui.md#where-is-my-mor)).

Use **Get MOR on Uniswap** on Status if you need a swap deep-link.

---

<!-- source: docs/03-gui.md -->

# 3. GUI basics

[← Bootstrap](02-bootstrap.md) · [Guide home](README.md) · [Next: Apps →](04-clients.md)

One topic at a time. You do not need every section on day one.

---

## Login

- URL: `https://<your-host>/gui/`
- User: `admin`
- Password: `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
- Two steps when 2FA is enrolled: password first, then the 6-digit code (or
  a recovery code). Wrong password and missing code get the same answer, so
  the page never reveals whether 2FA is enrolled; lockout and audit apply to
  both steps.
- Tabs: Status, API Keys, Probe, Sessions & Usage, Security (far right).
- Status, top to bottom: a status line (health or the reason it is not
  healthy, open sessions, versions), the four MOR numbers below, Connect a
  client, then Add MOR and Support (both collapsed). Hover or focus an &#9432; for help.
  There is no low-wallet warning: watch the Wallet number, and keep a
  little ETH on the wallet for gas (check it in your wallet app).
- Security: the **2FA switch** turns two-factor login on or off. It is off
  by default on every deploy (password-only login), and the tab shows a
  short note recommending turning it on; nothing is forced. Turning it on
  runs the enrollment: enter the admin password, start, scan the QR code,
  and confirm a code (the password is asked for again on confirm).
  Confirming signs out every other admin session; this browser stays
  signed in. Until a code is
  confirmed the tab shows one message, "Finish setup", and switching back
  off cancels the setup (after a reset, below, it cannot be switched off). 2FA is on once the code is confirmed, and 10
  recovery codes are shown once; save them.
  Each works once in place of the 6-digit code. The switch is stored in
  `DATA_DIR`, so it survives restarts and redeploys.
- Regenerate recovery codes, reset 2FA or turn it off from the same tab:
  the buttons (and switching off) need both the password and a current
  code or recovery code. Regenerate takes only a 6-digit authenticator
  code, not a recovery code.
- Admin sessions end after 4 hours without activity and 12 hours after
  login, whether 2FA is on or off; the Security tab shows both. Background
  refreshes do not count as activity. These lengths are fixed (no setting).
- Full API keys (copy, Probe, Export all) need a recent confirmation: within
  30 minutes of login or of the last confirmation. Otherwise the page asks
  for the password (and a 6-digit code when 2FA is on) and then continues.
- Turn off removes the 2FA secret and all recovery codes and signs out
  every session; the next login is password only.
- Reset wipes the 2FA secret and all recovery codes and signs out every
  session (you land on the login screen), but 2FA stays on. Log in with the
  password: only the Security tab shows, with a new enrollment and a new QR
  code, until it is confirmed; the old authenticator entry and old recovery
  codes no longer work.
- Locked out (lost authenticator and codes): emergency recovery is one
  restart with `UPLINK_RESET_2FA=true`, then remove it; 2FA comes back off
  ([details](06-developers.md#admin-2fa-and-recovery-codes)).
- **Settings** (collapsed, below 2FA): session length default and max,
  idle-sweep grace, the per-call idle timer and the log level. Save applies
  at once; Reset returns to the default. A value set in the environment is
  shown disabled with "set by environment (ENV)"
  ([Operator settings](06-developers.md#operator-settings)).
- **Security alerts** (below 2FA): the last 50 audit events (logins
  and lockouts, 2FA and key changes, boot session checks, provider
  failovers, balance drops),
  newest first. Each row reads time (local, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`) | event name
  (bold) | details, set as plain text. The filter box above the list hides
  rows that do not contain the typed text (case-insensitive). The list is
  loaded at boot from the audit files in `DATA_DIR`
  ([Audit streams](06-developers.md#audit-streams)), so it survives a
  restart; at least half of it is kept for admin and credential events. It
  loads once 2FA is enrolled or off; while an enrollment is required it says
  so instead.

---

## API Keys

| Kind | Survives a fresh deploy / volume wipe? | Role |
|------|---------------------------|------|
| **Master** | Yes (`API_KEY_SEED`) | Inference; admin API only with `MASTER_KEY_ADMIN=true` (default off), never on logout or 2FA status/enroll (cookie session only) |
| **Prompt** | Yes (`API_KEY_SEED`) | Inference only — default for clients |
| **Ephemeral** | No — export/import (kept across restarts and redeploys on the same data volume) | Named keys for apps/agents |

- Rotate built-ins by changing `API_KEY_SEED` and restarting. This also
  invalidates the 2FA secret and recovery codes; restart once with
  `UPLINK_RESET_2FA=true` to clear them, then remove it and enroll again
  ([details](06-developers.md#admin-2fa-and-recovery-codes)).
- Ephemeral: create, red trash to delete, **Export all** / **Import list**
  after a fresh deploy or a deleted data volume. A restart or redeploy on
  the same volume keeps them.

---

## Where is my MOR?

<a id="where-is-my-mor"></a>

![Where is my MOR? — Wallet → Active → On hold → To claim → Reclaim](assets/mor-buckets.jpg)

Opening a session moves stake from **Wallet → Active** (escrow for the full session duration). What happens next depends on **how the session ends** — not on how many tokens you prompted with.

| How the session ends | Liquid (back to Wallet on the close tx) | Time-locked (**On hold**) |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| **Close early** (GUI / housekeeping / router close before end) | Unused time portion of the stake | Used time portion |
| **Expire naturally** (session runs to its end time) | Nothing | **Entire** stake |

Then the clock:

1. **On hold** — daylocked until the next UTC midnight (`releaseAt`).
2. **To claim** — past `releaseAt`; ready to pull back.
3. **Reclaim** — `withdrawUserStakes` (Status button, or auto ~00:05 UTC) → **Wallet**.

| Bucket | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **Wallet** | Liquid MOR in the wallet |
| **Active** | Open session stake |
| **On hold** | Closed/expired stake still daylocked |
| **To claim** | Daylock done — reclaim to Wallet |

**Session stake (locks, not spends).** Stake is locked while a session runs
and returned to this wallet, held at most until the next UTC day. See
[02-bootstrap](02-bootstrap.md) for the full wording.

**Practical tip:** if you only need a short burst, close the session when you are done so unused duration returns immediately as liquid. If you leave sessions open until they expire, plan float for the **full** stake until the next reclaim cycle.

Deeper: [nodedocs — Where is my MOR?](https://nodedocs.mor.org/ai/where-is-my-mor) · [tech.mor.org/session.html](https://tech.mor.org/session.html)

---

## Sessions & Usage

- On boot Uplink lists the open sessions before opening any: still-valid
  ones are reused (one per model), expired and duplicate ones are closed so
  their stake is returned, and sessions for models not in the catalog are
  left to expire. The Status tab shows the last boot check and its counts.
  A graceful `docker stop` closes every open session on the wallet before
  Uplink exits, including sessions for models not in the catalog and, on a
  shared wallet, the other client's sessions; the stake is returned (a
  lock, not a loss). `CLOSE_SESSIONS_ON_EXIT=false` opts out. Use a
  dedicated wallet: the boot check and the stop act on every session of
  the wallet.
- A session with no call in flight and no use for 5 minutes
  (`UPLINK_SESSION_IDLE_GRACE_SECONDS`) is closed early so its unused stake
  returns. A session is never closed while a call is still running on it;
  apps can release their hold when done ([Long jobs](04-clients.md#long-jobs-timeouts-session-length-release)).
  `/admin/status` lists, per pool session, `inFlight`, `holderCount` and
  `holders` (key ids), `openedAt`, `endsAt`, `opener` and `long`.
- **Usage** counters are stored on the Uplink data volume: they survive
  restarts and redeploys, and reset on a fresh deploy or when the volume is
  deleted. Funds do not depend on them.
- Usage is counted per model registration: a call by name and a call by
  id to the same model land in one row, shown as `name (0x + 6 hex)`, for
  example `deepseek-v4-pro (0xb2c4a6)`. An id the catalog no longer lists
  shows its short id. Rows saved by an older version under a model name
  join the matching row when the name still resolves.

---

## Probe

1. Open **Probe**.
2. Pick a model (fuzzy search) and an API key.
3. **Run test**, or **Copy** the curl command.
4. Confirm a normal completion in **Response**.

---

## Logs & support

Router / container logs are **not** streamed into the GUI yet.

| Source | How |
|--------|-----|
| GUI Status | Health, version chips, MOR buckets, reclaim |
| Support JSON | Status → **Download support bundle** (no private keys) |
| Host logs | `docker logs <uplink\|proxy-router>` or your platform log panel |

# 4. Apps & agents

[← GUI](03-gui.md) · [Guide home](README.md) · [Next: Updates →](05-updates.md)

Uplink speaks **OpenAI-compatible** HTTP. Almost every OpenAI client works with three fields.

| Setting | Value |
|---------|--------|
| Base URL | `https://<your-host>/v1` |
| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer <Prompt or ephemeral sk-…>` |
| Model | Exact name from Probe / `GET /v1/models` / [`gateway_models.json`](https://active.mor.org/gateway_models.json) (not `active_models.json` / ALL) |

Prefer **Prompt** or ephemeral keys in clients; keep **Master** off machines you do not trust.

**Trust model:** every Prompt/ephemeral key can open sessions and lock MOR from
this gateway’s wallet. Do not paste keys into untrusted agents or shared
machines. See [DISCLAIMER.md](../DISCLAIMER.md).

---

<details>
<summary><strong>curl</strong></summary>

```bash
curl -s https://YOUR_HOST/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prompt.…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "model": "REPLACE_WITH_PROBE_NAME",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "In one sentence, what is Morpheus?"}
  ],
  "max_tokens": 128
}'
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Python (OpenAI SDK)</strong></summary>

```python
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url="https://YOUR_HOST/v1", api_key="sk-prompt.…")
print(client.chat.completions.create(
    model="REPLACE_WITH_PROBE_NAME",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
).choices[0].message.content)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Desktop / agent harnesses</strong> (Cursor, Continue, custom agents)</summary>

1. Create an **ephemeral** key (or use Prompt) in the GUI; copy it.
2. In the app: custom OpenAI base URL → `https://YOUR_HOST/v1`, paste the key.
3. Model string = **exact** catalog name from Probe / `/v1/models` / `gateway_models.json` (wrong name → resolve fails; never invent a flashy name).
4. After app updates, re-check base URL + key + model — Uplink’s contract stays OpenAI-shaped.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Errors and provider failover</strong></summary>

- When the model's provider fails (for example its backend is out of
  credit, rate limited or down), Uplink moves to another provider for that
  model and answers the same request; the client sees a normal reply.
  This happens at most once per request, and only when another provider
  serves the model.
- Otherwise the error comes back with its real status (for example `400`
  for a bad parameter, `402` or `429` from the provider when no other
  provider is available), in the OpenAI error shape (`error.message`,
  `error.type`, `error.code`). `502` means Uplink could not reach its
  router.
- Streaming: if the provider fails or its stream breaks off (no
  `data: [DONE]`) after part of the answer was sent, the stream ends with
  one `data: {"error":{...,"type":"provider_error"}}` event. Send the
  request again; the next one goes to another provider when the model has
  one. Closing your own connection is never counted against the provider.
- See [Provider failover](06-developers.md#provider-failover).

</details>


---

## Long jobs (timeouts, session length, release)

For calls that run for many minutes. All optional; without them nothing
changes. Use a generated `sk-…` key: the master and prompt keys cannot ask
for long sessions or release.

```bash
curl -sS https://YOUR_HOST/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-…" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Uplink-Request-Timeout: 1500" -H "X-Uplink-Idle-Timeout: 300" \
  -d '{"model":"…","stream":true,"messages":[…]}'
```

- `X-Uplink-Request-Timeout` (total seconds for this call),
  `X-Uplink-Idle-Timeout` (seconds without bytes, 30…600, default 180),
  `X-Uplink-Session-Duration` (session length for a new session, 600…max).
  Whole numbers only, sent once; a bad value is a `400` naming the header.
- The response then carries `X-Uplink-Timeouts: idle=…;total=…` and
  `X-Uplink-Session-Remaining`.
- A timeout before any answer is a `504` with `"type":"timeout"`. In a
  stream it ends with an error event, `finish_reason:
  "uplink_idle_timeout"` (or `uplink_total_timeout`) and `[DONE]`.
- Too many long sessions or opens → `429` `long_session_limit`; more than
  4 calls at once on one key → `429` `too_many_requests`.
- When done, release your hold so unused stake returns early:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://YOUR_HOST/v1/sessions/release \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-…" -d '{"model":"…"}'
```

  Answers `{"released":true,"closed":true}`, `…"closed":false,"reason":"shared"`
  (another key still uses it) or `{"released":false,"reason":"not_held"}`.
- Details: [Long jobs](06-developers.md#long-jobs).

## Usage (`GET /v1/usage`)

Poll per-key usage without the admin GUI. Same Bearer auth as other `/v1/*`
routes (Prompt, Master, or ephemeral `sk-…`).

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prompt.…"   https://YOUR_HOST/v1/usage
```

Response: `{"usage":[…]}` — rows with `day`, `keyId`, `model`, `requests`,
`promptTokens`, `completionTokens`, and optional `sessionSeconds`.

**WARN — scoping:** Prompt and generated keys see **only their own** rows
(`keyId` matches the caller). Master Bearer returns the **full instance**
(same table as `GET /admin/usage`). `keyId` is a public id (`master`,
`prompt`, or generated id) — never an `sk-` secret. Basic auth does **not**
unlock `/v1/usage`.

# 5. Updates & portability

[← Apps](04-clients.md) · [Guide home](README.md) · [Next: Developers →](06-developers.md)

---

## New Uplink versions

1. GUI header may show a **new release** chip when [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases) is ahead of the running build (notify only — you still apply the update on the host).
2. Download the new release compose (`docker-compose.secretvm.deployed.yml`, `docker-compose.generic.deployed.yml`, or for Railway the digests in `docker-compose.railway.deployed.yml`). Keep the **same** secrets / `.env` (`API_KEY_SEED`, `WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY`).
3. Export ephemeral keys **before** wiping storage if volumes recreate.
4. After restart: Status health → Probe once → reclaim if **To claim** &gt; 0.

---

## Upgrading from an earlier test build

Upgrades do not remove services that were dropped from the compose file
(`router-allowance-manager`, `router-user-init`) or their volumes
(`router_auth`, `manager_cred`, `allowance_status`, `allowance_ctl`). An
earlier test build may also have left an extra scoped router user in the
router's config.

- **SecretVM (production):** no shell (no SSH or serial access), so the
  only fix is a **fresh deploy**: a new VM with the release compose and the
  same six secrets. It clears the old services, volumes and router user.
- **Generic hosts and dev VMs:** do a fresh deploy, or clean up in place
  from the deploy directory (same `-f` / `--env-file` flags you deploy
  with; Docker prefixes volume names with the compose project name):

  ```bash
  docker compose up -d --remove-orphans
  docker volume rm <project>_router_auth <project>_manager_cred \
    <project>_allowance_status <project>_allowance_ctl
  ```

  Also delete `router.auth` from the Uplink data volume (`/data`), the
  router credential an earlier test build wrote there (the current build
  does not read it), and remove the extra router user, or do a fresh
  deploy if unsure; it clears both.

A fresh deploy starts with empty Uplink state. Generated (ephemeral) API
keys and the 2FA state (enrollment, recovery codes) are gone, and 2FA
comes back off. Master and Prompt keys come back from the same
`API_KEY_SEED`. Export ephemeral keys first and re-create or import them
afterwards, then turn 2FA on and enroll again.

---

## Portability

The portable unit is **published compose + env secrets + TLS terminator + public `:443`** (images from `ghcr.io`).

| Host | Pattern |
|------|---------|
| **SecretVM** | Release compose + encrypted `${}` secrets + platform certs |
| **Generic VPS** | Release compose + `.env` + Caddy |
| **Railway** | `deploy/railway/` scaffold with the release `docker-compose.railway.deployed.yml` digests + Railway Secrets; single-replica router |
| **Phala / dstack** | Same generic release assets + their secret injection |

Avoid baking RPC or wallet keys into the image — inject at runtime. Nothing requires SecretVM-specific APIs; only the Traefik cert mount is platform-specific (generic compose uses Caddy instead).

---

# 6. Developers

[← Updates](05-updates.md) · [Guide home](README.md) · [Root README](../README.md)

How the sausage is made — local runs, env vars, CI, repo layout. Operators
who only want to *run* Uplink can stop at chapters **1–5** and the root
[Get running](../README.md#get-running-secretvm) CTA.

---

## Key model (detail)

| Key | Derivation | Prompt (`/v1/*`) | Admin (`/admin/*`, `/node/*`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Master** `sk-uplink.…` | HMAC(seed, master) | yes | only with `MASTER_KEY_ADMIN=true` (default off); then the same power as the admin password, without 2FA, except the session-only routes below |
| **Prompt** `sk-prompt.…` | HMAC(seed, prompt) | yes | no — default for clients |
| Generated `sk-…` | random; hash stored | yes | no |

GUI login is `POST /admin/login` with `ADMIN_PASSWORD` (+ TOTP / recovery
code once 2FA is enrolled), which sets an HttpOnly session cookie; Basic auth
is rejected on `/admin/*`. The Master key can drive admin APIs as a Bearer
token only when `MASTER_KEY_ADMIN=true` (default off); each such request
writes an `admin_key_use` audit record (aggregated: the first use per
client address per minute is written at once, repeats become one
`count=N` line). The session-only routes
`POST /admin/logout`, `GET /admin/2fa/status`, `POST /admin/2fa/enroll/start`,
`POST /admin/2fa/enroll/confirm` and `POST /admin/step-up` require the admin cookie session: any
Authorization header is refused on session-only routes (any scheme or case,
empty or repeated, the Master key included) with the same 401 as a request
without credentials, whatever `MASTER_KEY_ADMIN` says.

### Admin sessions and step-up

- **Lengths** are fixed constants: idle 4h, absolute 12h, the same whether
  2FA is on or off. There is no environment variable or GUI setting for
  them. The cookie `MaxAge` is 12h; requests with `X-Uplink-Poll: 1` do not
  extend idle. `/admin/status` reports `adminSession` (`idle`, `idleSec`,
  `absolute`, `absoluteSec`, `stepUpMaxAgeSec`, and `warnings`, which holds
  the informational `2FA is off` while 2FA is off).
- **Step-up**: `POST /admin/step-up {"password", "code"}` (cookie session
  only, CSRF-checked, under the login lockout, checked before the
  password). With 2FA enrolled `code` must be a current TOTP code (a step
  works once); a recovery code is refused without being consumed. With 2FA
  not enrolled the password alone is checked. Success stamps the session
  and audits `step_up`. Credentials are read from the POST body only.
- **Key reveal**: `GET /admin/keys?reveal=1` returns full keys only on a
  cookie session that logged in or stepped up within 30 minutes; otherwise
  `401 step_up_required`. With any Authorization header it is `403`,
  whatever `MASTER_KEY_ADMIN` says; the masked listing over the Bearer is
  unchanged.
- **Client address**: a change of client address within a session is
  audited once per change as `admin_session_ip_change` (aggregated per
  session per minute). The session is not bound to an address.
- **Master Bearer lockout**: the Bearer branch of the admin routes has its
  own per-client-address lockout (5 free failures, then 2^(n-5) s up to
  15 min), checked before the key compare. It neither reads nor feeds the
  global login trip, so a password flood does not lock the Master key out
  from other addresses. Each rejected Bearer is audited as
  `admin_bearer_reject` (path and address only).

### Audit streams

Two JSON Lines files in `DATA_DIR` (directory 0750), opened append-only
with `O_NOFOLLOW`, mode 0600:

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `audit-security.jsonl` | Successful admin and credential events: `login`, `step_up`, `key_reveal`, `key_create` / `key_import` / `key_revoke`, 2FA changes, `setting_change`, a successful `session_open_long`, `pool_close` / `pool_close_all`, `admin_session_ip_change`, `admin_key_use`, `balance_drop` |
| `audit.jsonl` | Failures and agent or system events: `admin_bearer_reject`, login and step-up failures, other rejects, `session_release`, a refused `session_open_long`, `provider_failover`, `session_reconcile*` |

- **Aggregation**: unauthenticated failures (`login`, `login_lockout`,
  `admin_bearer_reject`) are written at most once per minute per (client
  address, event), and agent events per (key id, event); repeats become
  one line with `count`. The map holds about 10,000 keys; beyond that new
  keys share one `other` line per event. `admin_key_use` and
  `admin_session_ip_change` are aggregated the same way (64 keys per event).
- **Rotation**: at 5 MiB a file moves to `.1` and `.2`; at most 3 files per
  stream.
- **Retention**: `AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 90, 1…3650) for
  `audit-security.jsonl`, 30 days for `audit.jsonl`. Whole rotated files
  whose newest line is older are deleted at boot and daily; the live file
  is never rewritten.
- **Safety**: a symlink, a non-regular file or a file owned by another uid
  is refused (logged once; the in-memory list only). A write error is
  logged once and is not fatal.
- **Content**: `json.Marshal` only. Paths without the query, at most 256
  printable ASCII bytes; never the User-Agent, a token or any part or hash
  of one.
- **Boot**: the last 500 lines of each file are loaded into the in-memory
  list behind `GET /admin/audit` (same shape, plus `stream` and `count`)
  and Security alerts. Status `disk.audit` reports the file sizes.

### Admin 2FA and recovery codes

- **2FA switch** (operator choice in the GUI; no environment variable turns
  2FA on, on any deploy target). Stored as `auth.twoFactorOn` in
  `uplink-state.json` in `DATA_DIR` (mode 0640, atomic write like the rest
  of the state), so it survives restarts and redeploys. Default off: the
  first login is password only, and the Security tab shows a non-blocking
  note recommending turning it on. The switch and the confirmed TOTP secret
  change together, in one store update: enroll confirm stores the secret
  and sets the switch on; Remove wipes the secret and recovery codes and
  sets it off. Starting an enrollment does not turn it on. While on, every
  admin route and `/node/*` enforce the second factor exactly as before.
  Fail closed: login asks for a TOTP or recovery code whenever a secret is
  stored, whatever the switch says, and a state file that cannot be parsed
  stops Uplink at boot instead of starting with 2FA off.
- **`MASTER_KEY_ADMIN` parsing** (`internal/config`): unset, empty or blank
  means false; a boolean (`true`/`false`/`1`/`0`, surrounding space
  ignored) is that value; anything else stays false, logs one warning
  naming the variable (never its value) and shows it on the Security tab
  (`configWarn` in `/admin/2fa/status` and `/admin/status`).
- **TOTP** (RFC 6238, 30 s, one step of clock skew). The last accepted step
  is stored, so a code works once; replays get 401 (`bad_totp` or
  `totp_reuse` in the audit, never the code).
- **Recovery codes**: enrolling issues 10, shown once (copy, `.txt`
  download). Format `xxxx-xxxx-xxxx` from `a-z2-7` (12 symbols, 60 bits,
  `crypto/rand`). Input is case- and dash-insensitive. Stored next to the
  TOTP secret in `uplink-state.json` (same file, same mode) as
  HMAC-SHA256(pepper, salt || code) with a 16-byte salt per code; the pepper
  is derived from `API_KEY_SEED` with HKDF. Rationale in
  `internal/adminauth/recovery.go`. Matching is constant-time over every
  stored code and consumes the match inside one store update, so a code
  works once even under concurrent logins. Recovery logins share the login
  lockout (and, on SecretVM, the edge rate limit).
- **Endpoints** (CSRF and session rules as for other admin POSTs):
  `GET /admin/2fa/status` (`on`, `enrolled`, `need2fa`, `recoveryRemaining`),
  `POST /admin/2fa/enroll/start`, `POST /admin/2fa/enroll/confirm`
  (returns the codes), `POST /admin/2fa/recovery/regen`,
  `POST /admin/2fa/reset`, `POST /admin/2fa/remove`. Enroll start needs
  `{"password"}` and confirm `{"password", "code"}` (wrong password: 401
  `invalid password`, counted by the lockout); a confirmed enrollment
  revokes every admin session and re-issues the caller's cookie. Regen
  needs `{"password", "code"}` with a TOTP code only. Reset and remove need
  `{"password", "code"}`, where `code` is a TOTP or a recovery code.
- **Lifecycle.** Turn on (enroll): Security tab switch, scan the QR code,
  confirm a code; the 10 recovery codes are shown once. Regenerate:
  replaces all codes (password plus a code), shown once. Reset: below.
  Turn off (Remove): below. In the GUI, Regenerate, Reset and Turn off stay
  disabled until both the password and the code field are filled.
- **Reset** wipes the TOTP secret, all recovery codes and any pending
  enrollment, and persists that in one store update. It revokes every admin
  session (this one too), clears the cookie, and audits `2fa_reset` with
  `sessions_revoked`. The GUI drops to the login screen with the Security
  view cleared. The next password login goes straight to a new enrollment
  with a fresh secret; the old secret and old recovery codes never work
  again. The 2FA switch stays on, so every other admin route answers 403
  `2fa enrollment required` until that enrollment is confirmed, and the GUI
  shows only the Security tab. This enroll-only state is the one case where
  the switch is on without a secret; it grants nothing but enrollment.
- **Remove** (`POST /admin/2fa/remove`, the switch's off side) needs a
  valid session, CSRF, the password and a TOTP or recovery code (consumed;
  a TOTP step works once), under the login lockout. In one
  store update it wipes the secret and recovery codes and sets the switch
  off; then it revokes every admin session (this one too), clears the
  cookie and audits `2fa_remove` with `sessions_revoked`. The next login is
  password only.
- **Audit**: `2fa_enroll`, `recovery_codes_issued` (count),
  `recovery_code_used` (remaining count), `recovery_codes_regenerated`,
  `2fa_reset` (sessions revoked), `2fa_remove` (sessions revoked; `fail`
  with the reason on a rejected attempt). Codes and secrets are never
  logged.
- **`API_KEY_SEED` rotation** invalidates the TOTP secret (its encryption
  key is derived from the seed) and every recovery code (their pepper is
  too). With 2FA enrolled, admin login then fails until 2FA is cleared with
  `UPLINK_RESET_2FA`.
- **`UPLINK_RESET_2FA=true`** (emergency recovery, env only, default off):
  on the next start Uplink wipes the TOTP secret, all recovery codes, any
  pending enrollment and the 2FA switch (2FA comes back off), ends all
  admin sessions, clears lockouts, and audits
  `2fa_reset_breakglass` (`ok`, `wiped`). It then sets a marker, so later
  restarts with the variable still set do not wipe again; they audit
  `2fa_reset_breakglass` `blocked` and the Security tab asks you to remove
  it. Restart once with it set, then unset it and restart; that clears the
  marker for any future use. Log in with the password and turn 2FA on
  again with the switch. On SecretVM add
  `UPLINK_RESET_2FA=true` to the `uplink_bake_env` block (see
  [02-bootstrap.md](02-bootstrap.md)); on generic, Railway and local set it
  in the environment (`${UPLINK_RESET_2FA:-false}` in the compose).
- Logout and **Revoke all sessions** end the server-side session; there is
  no remembered device, so the next login asks for a fresh code.

### Soft revoke (tombstone)

`DELETE /admin/keys/{id}` **soft-disables** ephemeral keys: sets `revokedAt`
(UTC), clears `secret`, and **keeps** `id` + `name` (+ prefix/hash) so Usage
labels stay `Name (id)`. Auth via `LookupKey` treats revoked keys as unknown →
**401**. Revoking `master` / `prompt` is refused (**400**). Create/Import that
collides with a tombstone id or hash fails (**409**) — do not clear `revokedAt`
to revive; mint a new key.

**Orphan migration:** keys revoked **before** soft-revoke shipped were
hard-removed from `keys[]`. Their usage rows may show a bare hex `keyId`
forever — do **not** invent names. New revokes keep names. The Usage GUI
**Active** filter (default) hides revoked + orphan ephemeral rows; **All** shows
everything. Time range defaults to **7d** (UTC day buckets; no hourly precision).

### `GET /v1/usage` (self-scoped)

Bearer API keys only (`requireAPIKey`). Response `{"usage":[ row… ]}`, the
same row shape as `GET /admin/usage`:
`{day, keyId, model, modelId, requests, promptTokens, completionTokens, sessionSeconds}`.
Usage is recorded by the resolved registration id, so name and id calls
share a row. `model` is the display label `name (0x + 6 hex)`, or the short
id when the catalog does not list the id; `modelId` is the full id. Rows
stored under a model name by older versions are resolved and merged on
read; a name that no longer resolves is shown as stored with no `modelId`.

| Caller | Scope |
|--------|--------|
| Prompt / generated | Rows where `keyId` equals the caller’s id |
| Master | Full instance (intentional ops convenience) |

**WARN:** Master is a full usage reader so automation can poll without an
admin session. Prompt/generated never see other keys’ rows. `keyId` is public — not
`sk-`. Empty `X-Uplink-Key-Id` after auth fails closed (no unfiltered dump).
Basic auth on `/v1/usage` → 401. Keep `GET /admin/usage` for the GUI.

The proxy-router still has its own Basic-auth surface (`COOKIE_CONTENT`).
Uplink uses one full-power router credential and enforces Prompt vs Master at
its own layer.

---

## Other deploy targets

Same images; different compose. Assets from the
[latest release](https://github.com/MorpheusAIs/Morpheus-Uplink/releases/latest).

| Target | Compose | Notes |
|--------|---------|--------|
| **SecretVM (default)** | `docker-compose.secretvm.deployed.yml` | Encrypted Secrets; platform TLS |
| **Any Docker VPS** | `docker-compose.generic.deployed.yml` | `.env` + Caddy / Let’s Encrypt (`PUBLIC_HOST`) |
| **Railway** | `docker-compose.railway.deployed.yml` (reference) + `deploy/railway/` | Railway does not run compose: copy its digests and vars into the services; single-replica router |
| **TEE / compose clouds** | generic pattern | Phala / dstack fit here |

Step-by-step: [02-bootstrap.md](02-bootstrap.md). On SecretVM, Uplink bake
(`uplink_bake_env`) and router bake (`router_network_env`) are compose
`configs:` mounts -- not Encrypted Secrets. Keep them separate: never put
router `PROXY_*` / `LOG_LEVEL_*` into Uplink bake. Operator fillables are the
same six everywhere (`WEB_PUBLIC_URL` included).

## Local development

Not the production path. For hacking the Go service:

```bash
# full stack (needs funded wallet + RPC in .env)
cp .env.example .env
docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up --build
# Gateway: http://localhost:8080  ·  GUI: /gui  ·  Router: localhost:8082

# gateway only (against any reachable router)
export ROUTER_URL=http://localhost:8082 ROUTER_AUTH=admin:pass \
       ADMIN_PASSWORD=devpass API_KEY_SEED=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
go run ./cmd/uplink

go test ./...   # includes mock-router e2e (auth → session → chat → usage)
```
